places.name: Pesaro
places.what: Born to Giuseppe Rossini, a horn and trumpet player, and Anna Guidarini, later a professional singer.

places.name: Lugo
places.what: The family moved to Lugo; Giuseppe Malerbi taught him figured bass and composition.

places.name: Bologna
places.what: Enrolled at the Liceo Musicale in piano and cello; later studied counterpoint with Stanislao Mattei.

places.name: Venice — Teatro San Moisè
places.what: His first staged opera opened at the Teatro San Moisè.

places.name: Naples
places.country: Kingdom of Naples; Kingdom of the Two Sicilies from 1816 (now Italy)
places.what: Engaged by Domenico Barbaja for the royal theatres. This period includes Elisabetta regina d’Inghilterra, Otello, Armida, La donna del lago and Zelmira, with engagements elsewhere between productions.

places.name: Rome — Teatro Argentina
places.what: The opera opened under the title Almaviva, ossia L’inutile precauzione. Its first-night failure was followed by success.

sources.title: Rossini Opera Festival — Il barbiere di Siviglia

places.name: Vienna
places.what: Travelled with Isabella Colbran and the San Carlo company; Zelmira was performed at the Kärntnertortheater on 13 April.

places.name: London
places.what: Invited by the King’s Theatre management to direct his operas and write a new one; the planned Ugo, re d’Italia was abandoned after the management failed.

places.name: Paris
places.what: Appointed director of music and staging at the Théâtre-Italien.

places.name: Paris — Salle Le Peletier
places.what: The Paris Opéra presented his final completed opera, in four acts and in French.

sources.title: BnF stage-design record via Commons — Paris, Opéra-Le Peletier, 3 August 1829

places.name: Bologna
places.what: Accepted appointment as permanent consultant to the Liceo Musicale.

places.name: Florence
places.what: Prepared a permanent residence in Florence in 1850; left for Paris at the end of April 1855.

places.name: Paris
places.what: Returned with Olympe Pélissier. Their Paris home and villa at Passy became meeting places for musicians. He wrote the late Péchés de vieillesse and the Petite messe solennelle.

places.name: Passy, Paris
places.what: Died at his villa in Passy; his first burial was at Père Lachaise.

places.name: Santa Croce, Florence
places.what: His remains were reburied in Santa Croce after transfer from Paris.
